Hi Lena — welcome, and thanks for sending the W-9 and bank screenshot. A few items and next steps from our side:

1) Required legal name for vendor record
- Please confirm the exact legal entity name to appear on the W-9 (we copy this into our vendor master). Your W-9 looks like ClearStream Logistics LLC but we want the full legal string for contract/1099 purposes.

2) PO mapping (how Redwood expects invoices)
- Redwood's finance system looks for a PO value in a single text field on the invoice. Best practice is to put the PO as: PO# 2028-5512 (prefix with PO#). If your billing system only supports a short label, use the invoice field labeled "Reference" and prefix with "PO#".
- Example remittance mapping we prefer: invoice_csv column "reference" => PO mapping; column "invoice_number" => Invoice ID; column "total" => Line total. I’m attaching our vendor-onboard-template.csv for the columns we import.

3) ACH verification
- Either micro-deposits OR a bank statement + voided check is acceptable. Micro-deposits speed up the in-platform verification and avoid manual finance review. If you prefer micro-deposits we will initiate two small credits (low-value amounts) to the account you provided; please confirm the last 4 digits (you listed 5678).

4) Portal invite & docs
- I’ll send a portal invite (vendor portal link below) to complete the onboarding fields and upload any additional attachments (proof of insurance, certificate of incorporation if available).

Portal link: https://redwood.app/portal/vendor-onboard?token=inv-98a3
HubSpot vendor record: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/contacts/contacts/vid/98234

If everything looks good we’ll start the micro-deposit flow tomorrow and loop in FinOps for final enablement.
